label_kind: assistant-created engineering annotations; not independent human adjudication

expected_requests.intent: Replace the bare missing-score assertion with explicit validation that remains active in optimized Python.
expected_requests.note: The later comprehensive validation update is also an acceptable response, but the first author repair specifically acknowledges and fixes the omitted assertion.

expected_requests.intent: Make X/Y dimensions and lengths consistently validated before indexing or producing output.
Ensure the real Plotly encoding test actually runs in CI instead of being skipped without Plotly.
Move CLI coverage into the existing CLI integration test pattern and file.
Provide before-and-after screenshots for the UI change.
expected_requests.note: Polite phrasing still requests concrete visual evidence; do not remove or de-prioritize the existing tests from this comment alone.

non_request_sources.reason: Maintainer closure/inactivity announcement, not a concrete new author task; relevant context but not independently extracted work.

ambiguity_policy: Semantic scope and optionality are engineering judgements. Preserve original labels; record legitimate response alternatives transparently in separate scoring addenda. Possible response never proves code correctness or acceptance.
limitations: Six convenience-sampled recently updated reviewed PRs from one author and three organizations; not representative.
Discussions can have been encountered in earlier OSS maintenance; unseen means no ReviewRadar model evaluation output inspected.
Only five asks, all with a visible later author response. No no-response, partial-response, quotation-heavy or large-multiask capability claim can follow from this set.
Two PRs have only approval/thanks sources. This set is simpler than v10-fresh; its scores cannot be directly interpreted as the amount of improvement.
No category quotas or favourable-output filtering; fixed continuation of the previously frozen search order.
